Chapter 13
Engineering Change Management
Engineering change management and SAP S/4HANA change manage-
ment tools find extensive application in several SAP logistics and prod-
uct lifecycle management areas. These are essential tools to master
because they offer far better and in-depth controls to changes in the
master data than managing it through authorization controls.
Engineering change management and associated change management tools in SAP
S/4HANA offer extensive control in managing important master data in the QM area
and can be easily set up to bring better visibility and accountability across the busi-
ness processes. Engineering change management also has applications in other logis-
tics areas of the SAP S/4HANA system and enables users to appreciate and take better
advantage of the reporting features that are available.
This chapter begins with the important configuration needed to set up and integrate
engineering change management in QM, specifically for the task list (an inspection
plan). Then, it covers how you can integrate SAP Business Workflow with engineering
change management, with the engagement of an SAP Business Workflow consultant.
We’ll show you how to set up a user status profile and how it controls the business
functions. With the necessary configuration in place, we’ll move on to cover the change
master. A change master doesn’t offer as strong, elaborate, or comprehensive options
as newer SAP Fiori tools such as the change record, engineering record, and the man-
agement of change process do. Briefly, the chapter covers the following four change
management tools for master records:
 Change master
 Change record
 Engineering record
 Management of changes
Now, let’s begin with the necessary configuration in engineering change management
for the change master.

13 Engineering Change Management
586
13.1 Change Master
This section shows the configuration of the change master that begins with creating a
status profile and assigning object types to it.
13.1.1 Configuring a Status Profile (User Status)
Apart from the checks and controls that the system offers for the change master, it’s
also possible to control the flow of business transactions or incorporate greater con-
trols by maintaining a status profile in the system.
Note
Status profiles are used throughout logistics, so you can easily and quickly integrate them
with business processes. The concepts and details that we cover in this section apply to all
areas in which the SAP system provides the option to maintain the user status.
In engineering change management, maintaining the status profile has greater signifi-
cance in the change master record. To maintain the status profile, you need to first
define individual statuses within the profile, their positions with respect to each other,
and the business transactions that each status can control.
To create a new status profile, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Qual-
ity Inspection  Status Management  Define Status Profile. For this example, in the New
Entry dialog box (see Figure 13.1), set the Status Profile as “ECM_QM00”, enter a short
Text description, define the Maintenance Language as English (EN), and choose Con-
tinue to go to the Change Status Profile: User Status screen shown in Figure 13.2.
Figure 13.1 Initial Screen for Status Profile
In Figure 13.2, enter “1” for the Status Number, followed by a Status code of “CHEK” and
a short text. In addition, select the Init. status indicator to denote that this should
always be the initial status of the business function. Define the lowest and the highest
statuses for this status—that is, whether a lower status can be changed back to a higher
status. Repeat the same steps for the next status, which is APPR.

Maintaining the system profile for engineering change management enables the user
to maintain default values, which saves time and effort by reducing redundant entries.
To maintain the profile, follow menu path SAP IMG  Cross-Application Components 
Engineering Change Management  Maintain Profile.

13.2 Change Record
13.2 Change Record
Engineering change management with change records offers the flexibility to support
the management of engineering changes. It can handle several types of objects, such as
materials, material BOMs, and documents (from DMS) that are affected by the intended
changes. The engineering record keeps all information in one place. Status manage-
ment controls the entire progress of change, and the change process is also supported
by the workflow capabilities. Communication with SAP CoPilot during the change pro-
cess allows effective communication with all involved parties. Some of the key process
steps covered by change records are as follows:
 Determine responsibility
 Create change record
 Start workflow
 Approve change request (optional)
 Rework request
 Assign design document
 Assign material, BOM, and BOM items
 Approve or reject change request
 Modify validity date in the change master
 Perform design changes
 Perform material changes
 Perform BOM or BOM item changes
We’ll now create a change record with an example that will also simultaneously create
a change master (as already discussed in the previous section). The flexibility to create
a change master when a change record is created is controlled via configuration.
Note
The change record configuration can be found via menu path SAP IMG  Logistics –
General  Product Lifecycle Management (PLM)  Change Records.
13.2.1 Manage Engineering Changes
Figure 13.20 shows the Manage Engineering Changes app, which is accessed from the
Engineering Cockpit app. Once in the Engineering Cockpit app (shown later in Figure

up Figure 13.21.
As already noted, the different types of change records can be configured to meet a
company’s business needs. Figure 13.20 shows four such change record types.

13.4 Management of Changes
13.4 Management of Changes
Management of changes is a highly flexible and fully auditable process in SAP S/4HANA
for requesting, monitoring, and implementing changes. For example, a change request
can introduce a new chemical in the production process or modify operating condi-
tions of a piece of equipment. This change management tool can be used to do the fol-
lowing:
 Automate identification of risk experts, approvers, and subject-matter experts.
 Enable employees and contractors to request changes easily.
 Streamline the change process and drive forward consistency and standardization.
 Provide workflow and status management to ensure task completion.
A change request is a requirement for an adjustment to be made within a company, a
plant, or a process. When creating a change request, you first select the type of
changes involved. This change request type defines the details of a change request to
be queried—for example, related objects, activities, and questionnaires. A change
request can be used by anyone in the company or in the plant to report an incident
or a need for any improvement.
Figure 13.43 Change Request Types in the Configuration Menu Path

13 Engineering Change Management
612
The lifecycle of a change request starts as soon as the change request is created. It’s
based on the change request’s status network. This lifecycle can be managed by setting
the appropriate status. Further, you can also automate status changes so that the status
of the change request changes automatically when a certain activity has reached a cer-
tain status. To configure a new change request type in SAP S/4HANA, follow menu path
SAP IMG  Cross-Application Components  Management of Change.

several of these areas were already discussed in various sections and chapters of this
book. For example, Chapter 2 discussed catalogs and code groups, Chapter 3 discussed
digital signatures, and Section 13.1.1 discussed status profile maintenance (user status);
hence, these and associated topics aren’t repeated here.

13.44 appears.
Figure 13.44 Change Request Type

a change request, as well as for activities, are shown. The left side offers more options to
customize each change request type, such as assigning the previously defined digital

has been reached.

It’s important to understand how the predecessor-successor relationship for a status
network works in a change request. Table 13.2 shows that when a change request’s status
is In Preparation, the next and the only available status is Submitted. When a change
request is submitted, not only is the change request’s status automatically updated, but
with a Submitted status, the next four (successor) statuses become available: Awaiting,
Incomplete, Rejected, Not Applicable, and On Hold. As soon as the change request attains
one of these five statuses, the system makes available the corresponding successors or
next statuses, as shown in the Current Status column in Table 13.2.

13.5 Summary
This chapter covered the necessary configuration needed for successfully integrating
engineering change management with business processes. The user status (status
profile) has greater relevance in the change master. The engineering change manage-
ment information system provides in-depth and comprehensive details of all the
changes made and enables the user to select status-based information for further
necessary action. Newer master data change management tools to manage changes
in SAP S/4HANA are change record, engineering record, and management of changes.
The next chapter covers audit management in SAP S/4HANA.
